docs.title: OpenCDA-MARL
docs.text:
Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning for autonomous driving, built on OpenCDA: the same signal-free intersection scenarios run on CARLA (full vehicle stack) or on SUMO (traffic only, orders of magnitude faster), and any learner that implements one small contract trains inside the framework's episode loop with checkpoints, metrics and the experiment matrix included.

The web monitor's traffic view: a signal-free intersection during a live SUMO run, learning agents in blue — headless, no CARLA rendering.

docs.title: Four pages
docs.text:
• Quick Start

    Run a bundled learner untouched — SUMO, headless, monitor included — then change one thing.

  • Architecture

    One sealed lifecycle, many replaceable joints: the map of every plugin kind, port and config seam an experiment can swap or vary.

  • Run Experiments

    One run, the monitor, the experiment matrix: the launcher with parallel runs on a multi-GPU box, resume, evaluation and analysis.

  • Customize

    Plug in a learner (Add an Algorithm), swap a lifecycle joint (Replace a Component), or drive the scenarios from your own RL stack through the PettingZoo port.

Install first: Installation and CARLA Version Support. Developing the framework itself — as a person or a coding agent — starts at AGENTS.md (Contributing is the short form).

docs.title: What ships
docs.text:
• Learners: MAPPO, MASAC, MATD3, DQN and tabular Q-learning; PCMAPPO and PCMASAC build on PCMA (without its preference planner) for multi-objective training, and PCMATD3 is preference-conditioned only — all registered through the same interface an external package uses.
  • Baselines: the framework paper's DQN, MAPPO and SAC checkpoints and most of its TD3 ones (all but the two 1024-wide TD3-44d runs, which retrain from the td3_44d profile) ship in the wheel with their profiles and the deterministic recordings they were trained against — a fixed reference point for comparison.
  • Backends: CARLA 0.9.15 / 0.9.16 (0.10.0 experimental), SUMO via libsumo, CARLA–SUMO co-simulation.
  • Infrastructure: one verified lifecycle across backends with CARLA world reloads that carry the full learner state; resumable runs; a SQLite metrics store with a live web monitor and schematic traffic view; the experiment matrix launcher with per-slot CARLA servers and GPU spreading.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text: If you use OpenCDA-MARL, please cite the framework paper (and OpenCDA); the BibTeX is in the repository README. The preference-conditioned learners build on arXiv:2606.14693 (without its preference planner) — cite it with them (PCMA Learners).

docs.title: Validation Summary
docs.text:
• Local import probe passed for carla-0.9.16-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl.
  • Local import probe passed for carla-0.9.15-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl.
  • Local import probe passed for carla-0.10.0-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl.
  • The 0.9.15 + Python 3.12 wheel was built locally from the CARLA 0.9.15 source tag.
  • Full scenario regression is still pending, so the root Windows manifest should still be treated as an experiment default rather than a fully locked support baseline.
  • Linux (0.9.16 server + cp310 client wheel, Ubuntu 24.04) is validated beyond an import probe: MARL training runs (MASAC, PCMASAC, MAPPO, PCMAPPO and the path-action profiles) run to completion, single and four-way parallel with one server per GPU, through periodic world reloads, checkpoint save/resume, and both evaluation paths. No crash or core dump was observed across repeated server start/stop cycles.
  • The server binary is not packaged here: extract the official Linux release and point the launchers at it with --carla-bin /path/to/CarlaUE4.sh (or CARLA_BIN), or run it in Docker (scripts/docker_carla.py, see the MARL throughput page).
  • CARLA prints Disabling core dumps. during normal start-up on Linux — it is a UE4 status line, not a failure. A server that exits within a few seconds of start-up, leaving only that line, is almost always an environment problem rather than a CARLA bug: the known one here is SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen leaking into the server's environment, which UE4's bundled SDL2 does not support (the matrix launcher strips it).

The import probe checked the presence of symbols heavily used by the current project: command, TrafficManager, VehicleLightState, WeatherParameters, and LaneType.

docs.title: CARLA 0.9.16
docs.text:
0.9.16 is the main follow-up candidate for this repository.

  • The current codebase only contains explicit CARLA compatibility branches for older 0.9.11 and 0.9.12 blueprint naming differences.
  • No repo-level evidence was found that 0.9.15 depends on a deep API behavior that is absent in 0.9.16.
  • Python 3.10 is covered: 0.9.16 ships here as both a cp312 Windows wheel and a cp310 manylinux wheel (the Linux target pins Python 3.10 because of it).

Recommended validation targets for 0.9.16:

  • single_2lanefree_carla
  • single_town06_carla
  • single_town06_cosim
  • v2xp_online_carla
  • marl-quick-test

docs.title: CARLA 0.10.0
docs.text:
0.10.0 is intentionally tracked as an experiment, not a supported runtime.

  • Local import succeeded, which confirms that the Python module itself can be installed on Windows Python 3.12.
  • Current project support still looks mismatched at the feature level.
  • This repository depends heavily on Town05/Town06 flows, customized 2lanefree maps, Traffic Manager, SUMO co-simulation, V2X, and custom map import workflows.
  • CARLA's official 0.10.0 release notes describe multiple gaps in exactly those areas, so the project should not advertise 0.10.0 as supported yet.

Reference:

  • CARLA 0.10.0 release notes

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Contributions — by people and by coding agents — are welcome. The process is the one in Agent Workflow; this page is the short form.

Development here is specified agent-first: the canonical guide is AGENTS.md at the repository root, routing to the same Agent Workflow, Code Index and Conventions this site hosts. Point a coding agent at a checkout and it reads exactly the rules a human contributor does — one rule set, no drift.

Contributions are accepted under the Apache License 2.0 that covers the OpenCDA-MARL code (see LICENSE). Files from third parties keep their own terms; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

  1. Fork radar-lab/OpenCDA-MARL and branch from main (git switch -c feat/short-summary).
  2. Make one verified change. Tests ship with the change; pixi run pytest test -q is green; lifecycle, launcher and monitor changes get a live smoke run. Docs are updated on the page that owns the feature.
  3. Open a pull request against main with the PR template filled in — what changed, how it was verified, what you could not verify. Maintainers review and squash-merge.

Where things go:

  • A new algorithm does not need a PR at all: package it as described in Add an Algorithm and it plugs into the framework from outside. PR it only if you want it shipped as a built-in.
  • A new scenario or profile is a YAML file under opencda_marl/_bundled/configs/<family>/ that states only what it changes from the family default and scenario base.
  • A framework fix keeps the seams listed in the workflow page: one episode loop, registration instead of name dispatch, every opencda/ patch recorded in the patch ledger.

Bugs and proposals go to issues; include the scenario reference, the command, and the log lines around the failure.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Windows 10/11 (64-bit)
  • Python 3.12 for the root Windows manifest, or Python 3.10 if you intentionally select the backup manifest
  • CUDA 12.8 (for GPU acceleration)
  • CARLA 0.9.15 / 0.9.16 / 0.10.0
  • Git

Before installing, check the CARLA Version Support matrix and choose the Windows manifest that matches your CARLA wheel and Python ABI.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/radar-lab/opencda-marl.git
cd opencda-marl

docs.title: Step 2: Install Pixi
docs.text:
If you don't have pixi installed:

# Install pixi (Windows)
powershell -c "irm https://pixi.sh/install.ps1 | iex"

# Linux/macOS
curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh

docs.title: Step 3: Setup Environment
docs.text:
# Default root manifest on Windows: CARLA 0.9.16 + Python 3.12
# Alternative Windows manifests live in dependencies/pixi/
#   pixi_win_py310_carla0915_backup.toml
#   pixi_win_py312_carla0915.toml
#   pixi_win_py312_carla0916.toml
#   pixi_win_py312_carla0100_experimental.toml
#
# Linux remains on Python 3.10 because the bundled Linux CARLA wheel is cp310.
# Linux ROCm users should still use dependencies/pixi/pixi_Linux_ROCm.toml

# Install all dependencies
pixi install

# Test the installation: the test suite, the plugin registry, the SUMO
# bindings and a short SUMO run -- no CARLA server needed
pixi run verify

Windows manifest summary:

  • pixi.toml: default Windows experiment path CARLA 0.9.16 + Python 3.12
  • dependencies/pixi/pixi_win_py310_carla0915_backup.toml: backup CARLA 0.9.15 + Python 3.10
  • dependencies/pixi/pixi_win_py312_carla0915.toml: win-only CARLA 0.9.15 + Python 3.12, backed by a locally built Windows wheel
  • dependencies/pixi/pixi_win_py312_carla0916.toml: explicit CARLA 0.9.16 + Python 3.12
  • dependencies/pixi/pixi_win_py312_carla0100_experimental.toml: experimental CARLA 0.10.0 + Python 3.12

docs.title: Step 4: Install CARLA
docs.text:
1. Download the CARLA version that matches your chosen Windows manifest:
  2. 0.9.16 for the default Windows path
  3. 0.9.15 for the compatibility manifests
  4. 0.10.0 only for import-level experiments
  5. Extract to a folder (for example D:\Applications\CARLA_0.9.16, D:\Applications\CARLA_0.9.15, or D:\Applications\Carla-0.10.0-Win64-Shipping)
  6. Point the environment at it. The root manifest's Windows activation ([target.win-64.activation.env] in pixi.toml) sets CARLA_ROOT, CARLA_HOME and CARLA_BIN to the example location D:\Applications\CARLA_0.9.16, and activation overrides values set in your shell, so when CARLA lives elsewhere edit those three lines in pixi.toml (the matrix launcher also takes --carla-root / --carla-bin). Outside pixi, set the variable yourself:

$env:CARLA_HOME = "D:\Applications\CARLA_0.9.16"
4. [Optional] Download our customized pre-built maps package from Here and extract it into the matching CARLA_0.9.15 or CARLA_0.9.16 folder.

Linux servers: download the Linux release (CARLA_0.9.16.tar.gz from the official CARLA release bucket, ~8.3 GB) and extract it on a local disk (not NFS). The pixi activation expects /opt/CARLA_0.9.16; if it lives elsewhere, edit the [target.linux-64.activation.env] lines in pixi.toml (activation overrides shell values) or pass --carla-bin /path/to/CarlaUE4.sh to the launchers. The bundled Linux client wheel needs glibc ≥ 2.31 (declared in pixi.toml), and pixi install --locked needs pixi ≥ 0.73 (lock-file format 7). Keep the environment itself on local disk too: pixi config set --local detached-environments /local/path before pixi install when the checkout is on a network home directory.

Notes:

  • 0.9.16 is the main follow-up candidate for current OpenCDA-MARL workflows.
  • 0.10.0 is not a supported project runtime yet. Keep it limited to import and capability smoke tests until Traffic Manager, SUMO co-simulation, V2X, Town05/Town06, and custom map workflows are revalidated.
  • The root Windows manifest now points to 0.9.16 + Python 3.12 for ongoing experiments.
  • Keep dependencies/pixi/pixi_win_py310_carla0915_backup.toml as the immediate fallback if scenario regression reveals a 3.12 incompatibility.

docs.title: Step 5: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Run CARLA server (in one terminal)
cd $env:CARLA_HOME
.\CarlaUE4.exe
# Or manually start the server by clicking the CarlaUE4.exe file

# Run OpenCDA test (in another terminal)
pixi run marl-quick-test

Recommended Windows verification order:

  1. CARLA 0.9.16 + Python 3.12 root experiment path
  2. CARLA 0.9.15 + Python 3.12 compatibility manifest
  3. CARLA 0.9.15 + Python 3.10 backup manifest
  4. CARLA 0.10.0 + Python 3.12 import-only experiment

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
• CARLA connection errors: the server must be running before the client starts (CarlaUE4 -RenderOffScreen on a headless machine); the matrix launcher starts and restarts servers itself.
  • Perception with --apply_ml loads YOLOv8 from the ultralytics package (the pixi environment installs it; the yolov8m.pt weights download on first use). Only when that package is missing does it fall back to YOLOv5 through torch.hub; on recent PyTorch a cached models/common.py from before Ultralytics' fix then raises Expected 'device_type' of type 'str', got: '<class 'bool'>': delete the cached hub folder (~/.cache/torch/hub/ultralytics_yolov5_master) so torch.hub fetches the current YOLOv5 source, which passes the device type to autocast. That code is Ultralytics' (AGPL-3.0) and is not part of this repository.
  • A stale pixi environment after a lock change: pixi clean cache then pixi install.
  • libsumo import failed ...; falling back to traci: SUMO then runs over TraCI, about 13× slower per step. A pixi environment declares libsumo, so pixi install restores it. After a pip install of the wheel, install the binding that matches the bundled SUMO, as the warning says: pip install libsumo==<SUMO version> (the warning fills in the version of the SUMO binary it found). OPENCDA_SUMO_LIB=traci selects TraCI and silences the warning.
  • A system SUMO on the same machine (named by SUMO_HOME, or by a PYTHONPATH entry for its tools directory) is ignored while the environment's eclipse-sumo package is installed: the engine uses that package's binary and bindings and drops every other SUMO tools directory from sys.path, so the client and the server always match. SUMO_HOME is used only when the package is absent.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Run a bundled learner untouched, watch it live, then change one thing. Installation comes first — though for the SUMO path below that is just the repository and pixi install, no CARLA involved.

docs.title: 1. One training run
docs.text:
pixi run python opencda.py -t sumo-marl/intersection/route_speed_only_pcmappo --marl

That is PCMAPPO learning speed control at a signal-free intersection on SUMO — headless, around 10 ms per step, nothing to start beforehand. Starting the run starts the web monitor and prints its URL (http://127.0.0.1:8765): losses and episode summaries as they happen, and a Traffic view drawing the intersection schematically with the learning agents in it. Checkpoints, metrics and evaluation summaries land under artifacts/ (Run Experiments maps every output).

Swap the profile to change the experiment — route_learn_path_pcmappo adds the path action, marl/intersection/rule_based --marl runs a no-learner baseline on CARLA. opencda_marl/_bundled/configs/<family>/<scenario>/ lists what ships — the profiles are package data, so a pip install has exactly the same ones.

docs.title: 2. As a library
docs.text:
The engine is a wheel with the SUMO scenario family bundled, so an environment with the dependencies runs scenarios without a repository checkout:

pip install <opencda-marl wheel or checkout>            # SUMO runs out of the box
pip install "<opencda-marl checkout>[carla]"            # + libraries for CARLA runs from that checkout

pixi run wheel builds the wheel (dist/opencda_marl-*.whl); there is no PyPI release yet. The wheel's own CLI and environment port drive SUMO only. [carla] installs the libraries CARLA scenarios need when they run from a repository checkout (python opencda.py -t <ref> --marl), because those scenarios read their maps from the working tree; carla itself comes with your simulator. The faster libsumo binding is optional: without it SUMO runs over TraCI, about 13× slower per step, and the fallback warning names the matching pip install libsumo==<SUMO version>.

opencda-marl run -t sumo-marl/intersection/route_speed_only_pcmappo

opencda-marl list          # registered algorithms, and from where

The bundled configs are the last config root searched: --config-root DIR (repeatable) adds your own in front, and a profile placed there inherits the family default and scenario base from the bundle. That is the whole mechanism an external research package uses to ship its experiments — see Add an Algorithm.

The wheel also carries the framework paper's baseline checkpoints: MARL.training.load_checkpoint: ral/sac_300vph resolves inside the package, and opencda_marl/_bundled/checkpoints/ral/manifest.json lists every entry with the profile and recording it pairs with — a fixed reference point for comparing your own learner against.

docs.title: 3. Change one thing
docs.text:
Configuration merges three layers — the family's default.yaml, the scenario's base.yaml, then the profile — and a profile states only what it changes (a section left empty, such as outputs:, inherits the lower layers' block rather than clearing it). A new experiment is a new profile: it inherits the scenario (map, traffic, SUMO settings; the SUMO base runs headless) but names its learner's action space, objective and observation features, because those belong to the profile, not to the scenario:

# my_configs/sumo-marl/intersection/my_quick.yaml
# (the family default and the scenario base are inherited from the bundle)
scenario:
  simulation:
    max_episodes: 5

MARL:
  algorithm: "pcmasac"
  reward_profile: "competitive_intersection_v2"
  objective_mode: "competitive_ordering_v1"
  state_dim: 11                 # 9 features + 2 preference entries
  action_dim: 1
  action_space:
    mode: speed_only
  preference:
    profile: "balanced"
    assignment: "entry_direction"
    injection: "state_augmentation"
    dim: 2
  pcmasac:
    features:
      rel_x: 1
      rel_y: 1
      position_x: 1
      position_y: 1
      lane_position: 1
      heading_angle: 1
      dist_to_intersection: 1
      dist_to_front_vehicle: 1
      waypoint_buffer: 1

pixi run python opencda.py -t sumo-marl/intersection/my_quick --marl --marl-config-root my_configs

The scenario's base traffic with the observation of route_speed_only_pcmappo, a different learner (PCMASAC with its default hyperparameters), five episodes. Every knob the layers expose — action space, rewards, traffic, outputs — is mapped in Architecture; when the thing you want to change is not a knob but a component, that page's seam tables say which kind to register, and Replace a Component is the door: the mechanism on one page, a worked example per kind behind it.

docs.title: Run Experiments
docs.text:
Everything runs through pixi run from the repository root. One scenario reference selects a config family, a scenario and a profile:

<family>/<scenario>/<profile>      e.g.  momarl/intersection/learn_path_pcmappo
family backend what it is marl/ CARLA baseline agents (rule_based, vanilla, behavior) and the single-learner tutorial profiles pcma/ CARLA preference-conditioned speed control (MASAC / PCMASAC / MAPPO / PCMAPPO profiles) momarl/ CARLA the path + speed example family: one learner (PCMAPPO) under every built-in path provider; the profiles the matrix launcher runs sumo-marl/ SUMO the same intersection and learners without CARLA (route_* profiles) cosim-marl/ CARLA + SUMO co-simulation

Configuration is three layers merged in order: the family's default.yaml, the scenario's base.yaml, then the profile. A profile only states what it changes. A key left empty in a higher layer (outputs: with nothing under it, or null) keeps the lower layer's section instead of erasing it. Any other scalar, a bare true / false included, still replaces it; a mapping still merges into it key by key, and a list over it is an error; an empty value over a scalar or a list still sets it to null. Extra config roots (--marl-config-root DIR or OPENCDA_MARL_CONFIG_ROOTS) may hold just a profile and inherit the other two layers from the repository — that is how an external package ships its own experiment (Add an Algorithm).

docs.title: One run
docs.text:
# SUMO: nothing to start, runs headless in ~10 ms/step
pixi run python opencda.py -t sumo-marl/intersection/route_speed_only_pcmappo --marl

# CARLA: start a server first (see Installation), then
pixi run python opencda.py -t momarl/intersection/speed_only_pcmappo --marl
pixi run python opencda.py -t marl/intersection/rule_based --marl

What a run writes, under outputs.root_dir (default artifacts/):

path content checkpoints/<run>/<algo>/ latest_checkpoint.pth, best_checkpoint.pth, episode_NNNN.pth (pruned to keep_checkpoints every save_freq episodes), training_metadata.json metrics/<algo>/<run>/metrics.sqlite the metrics store read by the monitor (losses, Q values, episode summaries); <algo> is the registered algorithm key (masac, pcmasac, pcmappo, ...) <outputs.tensorboard.dir>/<algo>/<run>/ TensorBoard event files, in segment_NNNN/ windows of max_episodes_per_run episodes; when keep_last_runs is above 0 only that many newest windows are kept (the family defaults keep 5; 0 keeps all). dir is tensorboard in the marl/, sumo-marl/ and cosim-marl/ families and runs in momarl/ and pcma/; <algo> is the same registered key as the metrics store's, and <run> a timestamp unless outputs.tensorboard.run_name sets it metrics_history/<run>/metrics_history_epN.pkl full per-episode metrics archive, one pickle per export_interval episodes, flushed at exit evaluation/... per-episode summary CSV and final_summary.json when outputs.evaluation.mode: summary; the monitor shows the same numbers in the run's own entry (see Watch it) logs/<slug>/run.log the cell's log when launched by the matrix launcher recordings/<name>.json the traffic drawn by a mode: record run, named after replay_file's basename (outputs.recordings.dir moves it)

A built-in learner's checkpoint also stores a copy of its config, for reference only (nothing loads it back): plain values, without the tensorboard and metrics_store blocks that locate the run's outputs, and with any value that is an absolute path replaced by <absolute path removed> (a path inside a longer string is not). The hyperparameters are kept.

Key knobs live under scenario.simulation (max_steps, max_episodes), scenario.traffic (mode: replay|live|record, replay_file — the recordings under opencda_marl/_bundled/recordings/ are deterministic evaluation ground truth, and a record run writes its own draw to artifacts/recordings/ instead: adopting one as a benchmark is a deliberate copy into the package), and MARL.training (training_mode, save_checkpoints, save_freq, keep_checkpoints, load_checkpoint, checkpoint_dir). A baseline agent (rule_based, vanilla, behavior) on CARLA runs max_episodes like any other run. Every bundled family base sets 500, so a baseline profile that wants one episode says max_episodes: 1, as the bundled marl/intersection baselines do.

On CARLA, world.timeout (seconds; 20 in the bundled MARL families) is how long the client waits for the server on each call. Building an OpenDRIVE world or loading a town that times out is retried once with twice that timeout; a second time-out stops the run with a message naming the key, so raise it on a heavily loaded machine.

Evaluation is a run with MARL.training.training_mode: false and load_checkpoint: <path>: no learner updates, replay traffic, the configured number of episodes on both backends. A configured checkpoint that cannot be loaded aborts the run rather than scoring random weights. The framework paper's baselines ship in the wheel as eval-only weights: load_checkpoint: ral/<run> (e.g. ral/td3_43d_300vph) resolves inside the package, and opencda_marl/_bundled/checkpoints/ral/manifest.json names the profile and the traffic_<vph>vph recording each one pairs with.

SUMO → CARLA transfer is the same mechanism with training left on: train on a sumo-marl/ profile, then point a CARLA profile's load_checkpoint at the SUMO checkpoint. A loaded checkpoint marks the learner pretrained, so the random-action warmup is skipped and fine-tuning starts immediately. SUMO details live under world (sumo_gui: true opens the SUMO window, sumo_port when 8873 is taken).

docs.title: Watch it
docs.text:
Starting a simulation starts the monitor. Every run ensures a web service on http://127.0.0.1:8765 (a detached process that outlives the run and is reused by later runs; outputs.monitor: {enabled, host, port, allow_hosts}, or a bare true / false, controls it) and prints the URL. Manual start still works:

pixi run monitor            # http://127.0.0.1:8765 — every run under artifacts/
pixi run monitor-list       # the same, in the terminal

A Traffic view panel draws a live schematic of the selected run — SUMO-style lane lines, the learning population's vehicles as blue triangles and background traffic in grey — for headless runs on either backend, with no CARLA rendering involved (outputs.traffic_view: {enabled, interval}, or a bare bool, controls the writer). It shows the latest published frame, so it trails the simulation by up to one publish interval (interval, 0.2 s of wall time by default) plus the page's poll. When no newer frame arrives for max(3 s, 3 × interval), the last frame stays on screen dimmed and the status line reads stale; once the run has finished (its metrics store was closed after that frame) it reads run ended. A frozen frame is never labelled live.

The monitor reads the per-run metrics stores live (a training process never blocks it), overlays runs, smooths, and lists episode summaries:

  • One run, one entry. The run list labels each run <algorithm> · <mode>: the registered algorithm key (masac, pcmasac, ...), which also names the directory metrics/<algorithm>/<run>/, and train or eval. A learner run's evaluation statistics go into its own store: the Eval/* tags, one evaluation_episode event per episode and final_summary in the run's metadata. Only a run without a store of its own (a baseline agent, or a learner with outputs.metrics_store.enabled: false) gets a separate run under metrics/evaluation/, labelled with the learner key or the agent type.
  • Outcome columns first. Every built-in learner logs success_rate, collision_rate, timeout_rate and the vehicle counts successes, collisions and timeouts per episode, as external policies do. The episode table shows the outcome, throughput, TTC and near-miss columns first, then the reward_component_* columns, then whatever else the run logs in alphabetical order, up to 24 extra columns. Columns whose shown values are all whole numbers (counts, episode and step numbers) print as integers; other columns keep the page's usual precision on every row.

It is standard-library only, so it runs on a headless training node: ssh -L 8765:127.0.0.1:8765 <node> and open the same URL. TensorBoard event files are also written by default (outputs.tensorboard.enabled: false turns them off); pixi run tensorboard serves every family's under artifacts/, but the monitor does not need them.

One monitor serves one artifacts root: a run reuses a monitor only when it serves the run's own root, and when the port already serves another root the next port is tried, up to port + 7; the run prints the URL it got. The service outlives every run. To stop it, end the process whose pid GET /api/root reports; on Windows, stop it before deleting or renaming the root, which it holds as its working directory and <root>/monitor.log.

A monitor bound to a loopback address (the default 127.0.0.1) answers only requests whose Host header is a loopback name (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1], *.localhost), so the SSH tunnel above works unchanged. Behind a proxy that forwards under its own host name (Jupyter server-proxy, code-server /proxy, Open OnDemand, dev tunnels) the page gets a 403 host not allowed: NAME; start the monitor with --allow-host NAME. Start it by hand for that root:

pixi run python -m opencda_marl.telemetry.monitor --root artifacts --allow-host NAME   # repeatable

Later runs on the same root reuse it, because a run reuses any monitor that serves its root.

The store is on by default, for training and evaluation runs alike. Under outputs.metrics_store:

key default meaning enabled true write <root_dir>/<dir>/<algorithm>/<run_name>/metrics.sqlite dir metrics under outputs.root_dir (log_dir overrides with an absolute path) run_name timestamp the launchers set the cell slug log_frequency 10 stride for per-update scalars (losses, Q values); episode scalars are always kept 
from opencda_marl.telemetry import MetricsStore, discover_runs

run = discover_runs("artifacts")[0]                 # newest activity first
store = MetricsStore(run.path, read_only=True)
store.tags()                                        # tag, count, last step/value
store.scalars("Loss/critic", max_points=500)        # [(step, wall, value)], min/max downsampled
store.episodes(limit=50)                            # per-episode summaries

docs.title: Maps on both backends
docs.text:
A comparison of CARLA and SUMO wants the same roads on both, so derive the SUMO network from the CARLA map's own OpenDRIVE rather than building a lookalike:

pixi run python scripts/convert_opendrive_maps.py            # every map it can find

Converted networks live in opencda_marl/assets/maps/ with a README recording provenance. .xodr → .net.xml keeps CARLA's junction ids as SUMO node ids, so a site chosen in CARLA is findable in SUMO.

Pointing a scenario at an .xodr instead of a town name builds the world from the road network alone — no buildings or props, which loads in seconds and matches the SUMO network by construction:

scenario:
  map:
    xodr_path: "opencda_marl/assets/maps/Town10HD.xodr"

SUMO does not read scenario.map: it loads the network named by the <net-file> of the .sumocfg at runtime.sumo_cfg, so pairing the two backends takes a .sumocfg that names the derived .net.xml. On SUMO, a network derived from a CARLA map is read in CARLA's frame only with junction landmarks (runtime.coordinate_landmarks, or a <net>_landmarks.json beside the network; see the frame-convention row in Architecture). No .sumocfg names the derived town networks in opencda_marl/assets/maps/, and no landmarks ship for any town; without landmarks SUMO positions come out mirrored in y relative to CARLA's frame.

OpenDRIVE worlds skip pedestrian navigation generation by default. Vehicle experiments do not need a walker navmesh, and generating it on every world reload can leave expensive navigation-build jobs running alongside training. Set world.pedestrian_navigation: true when a scenario needs AI walkers. This setting does not change the road mesh or vehicle dynamics and does not affect prebuilt CARLA towns.

docs.title: Driver options
docs.text:
Traffic-signal behavior depends on the driver. For Vanilla-derived drivers, ignore_traffic_light: true disables the BasicAgent fallback light check. Explicit learned speed commands use a separate route-following path that does not call that check. A signalized experiment needs a driver or safety layer that also enforces signals for explicit commands. Verify signal handling on both backends when comparing them; sharing a map does not align it.

The bundled rule-based driver (RuleBasedAgent, CARLA) reads these switches from its driver configuration (agents.rule_based, over vehicle.behavior); the changelog lists how it differs from 1.x:

  • Forward corridor. Another vehicle is a leader only when its projected body overlaps the ego's forward driving corridor. A queue in an adjacent lane does not block a clear lane; vehicles merging into the corridor still constrain speed.
  • Junction yielding (junction_stop_on_conflict, on by default). A vehicle that must yield at a predicted conflict stops before the junction entry until the conflict clears, and the car-following speed cap stays active: granting priority to crossing traffic does not permit driving into a stopped leader.
  • Lane hold (lane_hold, on by default). The vehicle keeps its current lane, and drops back, while the planner's next lane is occupied alongside, instead of moving laterally into the occupied lane.
  • Merge order (lane_hold_geometry_priority, on by default). When nearby merging vehicles are standing and face the same direction, the front vehicle clears forward in its current lane first. They are ordered along their shared mean heading; positions within half a metre use actor IDs to break ties, and missing or incompatible headings fall back to ID order. false orders by actor ID alone, which can hold a merging vehicle and the standing vehicle behind it in place. The option does not bypass following, junction or other speed caps.
  • Abreast guard (abreast_guard, on by default). The rear vehicle of a same-direction pair alongside that is closing laterally drops below its neighbour's speed until the pair is no longer alongside.

An agent may expose a safety-filter state through a shield_state() method that returns a dict. Traces keep its applied_speed, shield_active, shield_stage, lane_hold and merge_priority_enabled, merge_priority_release and merge_priority_override fields, so behavior diagnostics can tell a speed the agent's own rules set from the commanded one, and an agent that reports shield_stage also says which rule set it. Only the CARLA vehicle adapter reads the hook. The bundled RuleBasedAgent implements it: lane_hold (the hold replaced the planner's target this step), merge_priority_enabled (the configured lane_hold_geometry_priority), this step's merge_priority_release and merge_priority_override, and applied_speed (the target speed its rules gave the controller; null on a step whose rules did not run). It has no safety filter, so its shield_active and shield_stage are null: its trace separates lane holding, but not following from junction yielding. The other bundled agents (marl, vanilla, behavior) do not implement the hook, so their vehicles, the learner's marl vehicles included, record null in all seven fields. For a vehicle the learner does not command, the record's target_speed is the vehicle's current speed, so the gap to applied_speed is not an intervention. On SUMO every field is null: SUMO builds no driver agent, the learner commands its vehicles' speeds through TraCI, and background populations such as rule_based stay on SUMO's own car-following and lane-change models. CARLA collision events also include the actual other actor's ID/type, event frame and impulse in metadata, distinguishing vehicle contacts from static geometry without changing the collision threshold.

docs.title: The experiment matrix
docs.text:
scripts/experiments/launch_matrix.py plans conditions × regimes × seeds as cells, writes one runtime profile per cell under artifacts/_runtime/ (passed to each run as an extra config root), and runs them — sequentially or in parallel slots, each slot with its own CARLA server:

pixi run python scripts/experiments/launch_matrix.py \
    --conditions speed_only_pcmappo learn_path_pcmappo \
    --regimes aligned --seeds 0 1 \
    --max-episodes 10 --parallel 2 --resume
  • --resume skips cells whose archive already holds --max-episodes episodes and restarts interrupted cells from their latest_checkpoint.pth with continuous episode numbering and the pre-interruption best preserved.
  • --cell-timeout kills the whole cell process tree; a failed cell bounces only its own CARLA server; the launcher exits non-zero when any cell failed.
  • --parallel N runs N slots on RPC ports 2000 + 10k; --cuda-visible-devices and --carla-gpus spread learners and servers over the cards (slot k takes entry k mod n). Servers the launcher started are stopped at exit (--keep-carla to keep them).
  • --carla-restart-mode process --carla-bin /path/to/CarlaUE4.sh uses a host binary; docker restarts pre-started opencda-carla-<port> containers (Throughput has the Docker recipe and measured multi-GPU numbers).
  • The default --carla-restart-mode process starts and restarts CARLA itself, so it needs CARLA_ROOT (or --carla-root / --carla-bin / CARLA_BIN); with servers managed elsewhere pass --carla-restart-mode none (or docker).
  • --partition k/n takes every n-th cell starting at k (stride slicing), so n machines sharing one artifact tree each run one partition of the same plan.
  • --slug-prefix (default matrix_) names the run: every cell slug is <prefix><map>_<condition>_<regime>_seed<N>, and --resume only matches cells under the active prefix. Continuation cells (continue_*) start from the same prefix's source cells unless --continue-source-prefix names another run.
  • --maps names map profiles (default custom), and <map> in a slug is always the profile's key. --maps, --continue-source-map and launch_eval_matrix.py --checkpoint-map accept any case, so --maps Custom names matrix_custom_* cells. Spellings of one map (--maps custom Custom) plan its cells once, and an unknown map stops the launcher before any cell is planned.
  • --dry-run prints the plan and the exact commands.

pixi run matrix …, pixi run matrix-eval … and pixi run matrix-analyze are shorthands for the three scripts; extra arguments are appended.

Then evaluate and summarise:

# replay-traffic evaluation of every cell's best checkpoint, isolated under *_eval200vph slugs
pixi run python scripts/experiments/launch_eval_matrix.py --conditions ... --regimes ... --seeds ... --eval-episodes 3

# or the checkpoint-eval route, which writes eval_summary.json per cell
pixi run python scripts/experiments/run_matrix_eval.py --episodes 3

pixi run python scripts/experiments/analyze_matrix_results.py   # training outcomes per cell / action space / regime
pixi run python scripts/experiments/analyze_matrix_eval.py      # evaluation outcomes

Each analyzer and run_matrix_eval.py reads every slug prefix under its root and prints the prefix in each row; pass --slug-prefix <prefix> to read or evaluate one run (they warn when several are present).

Several machines: launch_distributed_matrix.py --manifest workers.yaml partitions the plan over the workers described in scripts/experiments/workers.example.yaml.

The launcher is wired to the bundled CARLA momarl/intersection family. SUMO runs need no CARLA server: run sumo-marl/ profiles directly (pixi run python opencda.py -t sumo-marl/intersection/<profile> --marl, about 10 ms per step), as many processes as you have cores.

docs.title: Verify before you trust a number
docs.text:
• A learner that never acted produces plausible summaries: read the learner's own counters (training_step, updates_performed, buffer size) in the monitor or the log, not the episode summary alone.
  • Compare speeds back-to-back on the same machine state; absolute ms/step drifts 2–3× with background load.
  • Seeded outcome numbers are not comparable across commits that change numerics at the ulp level; the runs are chaotic. Semantics are pinned by tests, not by outcome numbers.

Guide version 1.1 — OpenCDA-MARL 2.1 (2026-10)

Open this when you need to find where something lives, how a run executes, or which seam a change belongs to. Every path below exists in the repository (a test checks), so the index is a map you can trust rather than a narrative. The edit policy per area is in the Agent Workflow.

The package tree states the architecture, and a test enforces it (test/basic/test_architecture.py):

opencda_marl/
  _kernel/      the complete lifecycle — SEALED. Never imports a plugin;
                external code never imports it. Everything replaceable is
                reached through api/ and the plugin registry.

  builtin/      the framework's own plugin set: default implementations

docs.text:
opencda.py -t <family>/<scenario>/<profile> --marl
 └─ opencda_marl/utils/config_locator.py     resolve default.yaml → base.yaml → profile (+ extra roots)
 └─ opencda_marl/utils/config_merger.py      smart_merge of the three layers (an empty key keeps the lower layer's mapping)
 └─ opencda_marl/_kernel/lifecycle/coordinator.py    MARLCoordinator(config) turns null top-level sections into {}
     │    (normalize_run_config), then initialize() → run()
     │    plugins load (entry points, $OPENCDA_MARL_PLUGINS, MARL.plugins, contrib),
     │    every part constructs through the registry, then the registry FREEZES
     ├─ CARLA: _kernel/lifecycle/pipeline_builder.py builds
     │    MARLScenarioManager (_kernel/lifecycle/scenario_manager.py)  CARLA client, world, CavWorld
     │    MARLManager          (_kernel/policy/manager.py)             observations → policy → rewards
     │    MARLEnv              (_kernel/envs/marl_env.py)              the CARLA episode
     │    WorldManager         (_kernel/lifecycle/world_manager.py)    periodic world reloads with state carry-over
     └─ SUMO:  SumoMARLEnv    (_kernel/envs/sumo_marl_env.py)         the whole backend in one class (libsumo/traci)
 └─ one step (coordinator.step):
      env.step → MARLTrafficManager spawns / retires vehicles (_kernel/traffic/traffic_manager.py)
               → MARLAgentManager drives each vehicle's agent (_kernel/agent_manager.py)
               → MARLManager.extract states (the observation_extractor plugin) → algorithm.select_action(s)
               → the reward_calculator plugin (api/rewards.py resolves profiles) → objective vectors (api/objectives.py)

      EvaluationManager.end_episode (evaluation/manager.py) → CheckpointManager (_kernel/policy/checkpoint.py)
      → MARLManager.reset_episode → env.reset

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text:
Everything goes through opencda_marl.api; python -m opencda_marl.plugins lists what is registered and from where. The user-facing map of the same seams — contracts, doors, config keys, built-ins — is Architecture; keep the two in step.

you want to… touch add a learner nothing inside the framework: drop a module into opencda_marl/builtin/algorithms/contrib/ (cloned repo) or ship a package with an opencda_marl.plugins entry point — Add an Algorithm drive the scenarios from your own RL loop opencda_marl/envs/parallel_env.py add a planner / agent type / reward calculator / observation extractor / intent provider register_component (opencda_marl.api) in your package; select with scenario.traffic.planner.type, agents.agent_type, MARL.components.<kind> add a reward / objective / preference profile register_reward_profile / register_objective_profile / register_preference_profile (opencda_marl.api) invent a new axis register_component("your_kind", "your_key") — unknown kinds are accepted and listed run mixed autonomy agents.population: {mix: {marl: 0.5, rule_based: 0.5}, seed: N} — shares exact over each window of resolution vehicles, reproducible per seed; the learner commands and learns from its own population only. The mix must name agents.agent_type; on CARLA it is validated at construction (no learning population: rejected; zero learner share: warning; every positive-share name must be a registered agent type, case-sensitive). On SUMO only that population gets the RL runtime mode and a commanded speed; every other population keeps SUMO's safeguards and car-following model swap the neighbour-context encoder MARL.<algo>.context_encoder: <registered key> (default lstm); a context_encoder component implements forward / forward_padded over the ego-first neighbour sequence give a vehicle its own driver parameters put them in the spawn event's metadata.driver; the agent factory receives the whole block as config["spawn_metadata"], and SUMO applies the known keys to background vehicles fix the SUMO frame convention for a map runtime.coordinate_landmarks (or a <net>_landmarks.json / <net>_junction_graph.json beside the network, keyed by junction id as {"12": [x, y]} or {"junctions": {"12": {"centre": [x, y]}}}): junction centres in CARLA's frame decide y_flip; a map without landmarks is read with no y flip, so a CARLA town export needs them give vehicles per-vehicle objective preferences agents.preference: {mode, sampler, dim, alpha, seed, regime} — the canonical home (moved out of route_intent, where the legacy location still resolves) choose what one path action means MARL.action_space.path.provider: <registered intent_provider>; the built-in semantic action (left / straight / right / keep) is the framework's example, and selector: learned \| rule_based \| random_legal \| keep_current still names the built-ins decide at the junction instead of at spawn MARL.action_space.path.decision_zone: {trigger: approach, distance_m: 30} observe neighbours' committed exit lanes MARL.<algo>.features.committed_exit_lanes: <width> (off by default; the state width changes with it) add a scenario or profile a YAML under opencda_marl/_bundled/configs/<family>/<scenario>/ stating only what changes — or the same path under your own --marl-config-root add a traffic recording record mode writes one under artifacts/recordings/; copy it into opencda_marl/_bundled/recordings/ to adopt it as a benchmark — the packaged files are evaluation ground truth add a monitor chart type opencda_marl/telemetry/static/ (vanilla JS, no build step) against the /api/runs/... endpoints in monitor.py feed the live traffic view from a new backend implement collect_traffic_view() / collect_traffic_geometry() on the env (opencda_marl/telemetry/traffic_view.py documents the file shapes)

docs.title: Configs
docs.text: The families are package data, under opencda_marl/_bundled/configs/: <family>/default.yaml → <family>/<scenario>/base.yaml → <family>/<scenario>/<profile>.yaml, merged by opencda_marl/utils/config_merger.py. Families: marl/ (baselines, tutorials, the RAL-era learners), pcma/ (preference-conditioned speed control on CARLA), momarl/ (the path + speed example family on CARLA), sumo-marl/ (the SUMO equivalents), cosim-marl/, and opencda/ (the classic OpenCDA scenarios for standard mode). Resolution order: explicit roots (--marl-config-root, OPENCDA_MARL_CONFIG_ROOTS), a checkout-level configs/ if one exists, the bundle last. The matrix launcher writes its per-cell profiles under artifacts/_runtime/ and passes that as an extra root. opencda_marl/tools/config_lint.py checks every shipped profile statically (test/basic/test_config_lint.py); test/basic/test_bundled_data.py pins the layout. docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Guide version 1.1 — OpenCDA-MARL 2.1 (2026-10)

Open this when naming something, bumping the version, or checking whether an oddity you hit is already a known issue. The behaviour rules are in Agent Workflow; the map is the Code Index.

  • Naming
  • Versioning
  • Known issues

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
• Scenario references: <family>/<scenario>/<profile> with families marl/, pcma/, momarl/, sumo-marl/, cosim-marl/. SUMO route-intent profiles are opencda_marl/_bundled/configs/sumo-marl/intersection/route_*.yaml.
  • Commit scopes in use: feat(marl), fix(traffic), perf(sac), docs(marl), test(route_intent), chore(repo), and similar.
  • momarl, pcma, the aligned / conflicting regimes and the artifact slug shapes are feature names and part of the experiment vocabulary — renaming one is an API decision, not cleanup. registry.label (and the rest of register_algorithm's signature) is documented public API; renaming it is a breaking change.
  • Adding an algorithm must never require editing opencda_marl/: register it and declare capabilities. If a new dispatch site seems to need a name list or isinstance check, the capability is missing — add it instead.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
• major.minor.revision. A verified patch-level fix bumps revision in the same commit that lands it; features bump minor, breaking changes bump major.
  • The version is declared in three places that must agree — pixi.toml (version), opencda_marl/__init__.py (__version__) and CITATION.cff (version). test/basic/test_docs_boundary.py checks that they do; bump all three together.

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
Open items a contributor may hit; do not "fix" one by weakening an assertion.

  • Suite baseline: measure it with pixi run pytest test -q rather than trusting a recorded count; the expected skips are CUDA-graph headroom and live-CARLA cases.
  • Console encoding: anything printed on the entry path (banners, launcher status) stays ASCII. A Windows console whose code page is not UTF-8 raises UnicodeEncodeError at startup on any other character — that error is this, not a logic bug.
  • Torch import order: opencda.py imports torch before the MARL runtime, and opencda_marl.builtin.algorithms registers its learners lazily (a learner module loads only when its factory is called), because importing a learner module before torch in a fresh process can fault while Windows loads torch's DLLs. New entry points and tests keep that order: torch first.
  • Planner hard-coding: opencda_marl/builtin/planning/local_planner.py (get_current_lane) and opencda/core/plan/local_planner_behavior.py (max_acc = 3.5, "hard-coded, need to be tuned").
  • SAC/TD3 soft-update tau is duplicated per family (opencda_marl/builtin/algorithms/sac.py, td3.py).
  • SUMO spawn backpressure: SumoMARLEnv active-agent sync under heavy traffic (see max_active_agents).
  • Deferred by choice in the vendored core: weakref.ref(x)() immediate-deref sites (opencda/core/safety/safety_manager.py, v2x_manager.py, platooning_manager.py) and stray world.tick() ownership at episode/reload boundaries.
  • On CARLA, vehicles that time out have their route intents finalised after the episode's intent diagnostics were snapshotted, so those counters lag one episode.

Guide version 1.1 — OpenCDA-MARL 2.1 (2026-10)

Open this before changing code: it is how changes are made to OpenCDA-MARL, written for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, …) and applying equally to people. Read it with the Code Index, which maps where things live, and Conventions for naming, versioning and known issues. Nothing here is decorative — each rule exists because its absence cost a debugging session.
